Orthopedics · published research

Back pain

A 148-person sham-controlled trial found no added improvement in pain or disability, and smaller trials combining PBM with exercise or home treatment also report mixed or null between-group results.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A 148-person sham-controlled trial found no added improvement in pain or disability, and smaller trials combining PBM with exercise or home treatment also report mixed or null between-group results.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Pain > Back pain category contains 67 unique titles: 52 human clinical publications, five systematic reviews, five meta-analyses, five protocols, one cost analysis, and one commentary. The review types overlap with study-design classifications. The category includes conventional PBM, LED devices, high-intensity laser therapy, and laser acupuncture, which are not interchangeable interventions.

Human and clinical evidence

A 148-person sham-controlled randomized trial found that laser therapy was not superior to placebo for back pain or disability (Guimarães et al. 2021). In a 38-person trial, adding PBM to Pilates did not improve outcomes beyond Pilates alone (Merlo et al. 2024). A small home-treatment trial also reported no significant between-group differences in its main clinical outcomes (Wang et al. 2025). Some smaller studies report improvement, particularly in combination programs, but the direct evidence does not show a consistent advantage over sham or active rehabilitation.

Animal evidence

No animal study was identified in this exact back-pain category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified in the exact category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols include multiband 640, 875, and 905-nm treatments over 12 visits in four weeks; red and near-infrared PBM around Pilates sessions; and home devices combining several wavelengths over multiple weeks. High-intensity laser and laser acupuncture studies use distinct delivery methods and should not be merged with conventional low-level PBM. Differences in schedule, comparator, and co-intervention limit pooling.

Interpretation

Some reports show improvement, but the largest sham-controlled comparison and several adjunct trials do not show added benefit. Current evidence does not establish a durable or general effect across chronic back-pain presentations.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term back-pain reduction with selected adjunct regimens Very low for consistent functional or durable benefit across back-pain populations
Publications and records67 unique titles in the exact category

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category includes 52 human clinical publications, but protocols range from conventional PBM to high-intensity laser and laser acupuncture. A large sham-controlled trial and smaller adjunct trials report null or mixed results. Larger, well-matched sham trials with standardized pain and disability outcomes would clarify which subgroups, if any, benefit.
